tracks.narration: A swinging weight and a flowing current — could they really obey the same rule?
The pendulum swings back and forth, and the current in the circuit sloshes between coil and capacitor in exactly the same rhythm.
Position becomes charge, velocity becomes current, mass becomes inductance, and spring stiffness becomes one over capacitance.
Both systems obey the same second-order differential equation. The natural frequency for the pendulum is the square root of k over m, and for the circuit, one over the square root of L times C.
Add resistance to the circuit or friction to the pendulum — both decay, and the amplitude falls exponentially toward zero.
Same math, different physics. Once you understand one, you understand the other.
